Package com.bilt.pos.widget

Class WebSurface

java.lang.Object
com.bilt.pos.widget.WebSurface
All Implemented Interfaces:
Surface
public abstract class WebSurface extends Object implements Surface
A Surface that draws through a browser control the register already embeds.

The SDK has no dependency on any platform's WebView. A register subclasses this class and wires three things to its own control: loadUrl(java.lang.String) navigates it, evaluateJavascript(java.lang.String) runs a script in the loaded page, and the platform's JavaScript interface (an addJavascriptInterface object on Android, a WKScriptMessageHandler on iOS, a CEF query handler on desktop) forwards each string the page posts to onBridgeMessage(java.lang.String). Everything else — the bridge protocol, ready-gating, token checks — is implemented here once.

Bridge protocol

Outbound, the SDK calls window.BiltMedia.receive(message) on the page with one of: 


 { "type": "rendering", "rendering": { "creativeId": "crt_91ad", "placement": "lane-banner",
     "media": { "type": "video", "url": "https://...", "durationMs": 15000, "poster": "https://..." },
     "headline": "...", "body": "...",
     "cta": { "label": "Apply offer", "action": "APPLY_OFFER", "token": "act_..." },
     "secondary": { "label": "Text me this", "action": "SEND_TO_PHONE", "token": "act_..." },
     "ttlMs": 30000, "tracking": { "impression": "https://...", "viewability": "https://..." } } }
 { "type": "clear" }

Inbound, the page posts one of: 


 { "type": "ready" }
 { "type": "action", "creativeId": "crt_91ad", "action": "APPLY_OFFER", "token": "act_..." }
 { "type": "viewed",    "creativeId": "crt_91ad" }
 { "type": "dismissed", "creativeId": "crt_91ad" }
 { "type": "completed", "creativeId": "crt_91ad" }

Both directions are specified by /com/bilt/pos/widget/bridge-messages.schema.json on the SDK's classpath. Inbound messages are allow-listed by type; an action must name the creative currently on display and carry one of its own CTA tokens, and viewed, dismissed and completed must name the current creative. Only the first viewed for each shown rendering counts, so a page that reloads and sees the rendering again cannot report a second view. A rendering's TTL runs from the show(com.bilt.pos.widget.Rendering, com.bilt.pos.widget.ActionSink) that delivered it; once it has passed, the rendering's CTAs are no longer acted on even if the widget's replacement or clear has not yet arrived. Anything else — malformed JSON, an unknown type, a foreign or stale token, an expired CTA, a repeated view — is dropped and reported through onBridgeError(java.lang.String, java.lang.String), never thrown into the platform callback and never passed to the ActionSink.

Lifecycle

The renderer page is loaded lazily on the first show(com.bilt.pos.widget.Rendering, com.bilt.pos.widget.ActionSink). Until the page posts ready, the latest rendering (or a clear) is held and pushed once the page announces itself; after that, shows and clears are evaluated directly. A page that reloads and posts ready again receives the current rendering again, so a browser crash or navigation heals itself, unless that rendering's TTL has passed, in which case the page is left empty for the widget's next show. A host that preloads the page before the first show simply forwards the early ready.

Threading

show(com.bilt.pos.widget.Rendering, com.bilt.pos.widget.ActionSink) and clear() arrive on the widget's executor, onBridgeMessage(java.lang.String) on whatever thread the platform delivers JavaScript messages on. The class serializes its own state and calls loadUrl(java.lang.String), evaluateJavascript(java.lang.String) and the sink with no lock held. Outbound calls are issued one at a time in the order of the state changes that produced them, even when a ready races a show or clear; a subclass is responsible for marshaling them, in that order, to the thread its browser control requires and should return without waiting for the result.

  • Method Details

    • loadUrl

      protected abstract void loadUrl(String url)
      Navigates the browser control to url. Called with no lock held; may be asynchronous. If it throws, the next show tries the load again.

    • evaluateJavascript

      protected abstract void evaluateJavascript(String script)
      Runs script in the loaded page. Called with no lock held; may be asynchronous.

      If this or loadUrl(java.lang.String) throws, the calls queued behind it still run and the first exception is rethrown to whichever caller was sending the queue: the show(com.bilt.pos.widget.Rendering, com.bilt.pos.widget.ActionSink) or clear() that queued it, or a concurrent bridge callback, which reports it through onBridgeError(java.lang.String, java.lang.String).

    • onBridgeError

      protected void onBridgeError(String reason, String rawJson)
      Called for every inbound message the bridge drops: malformed JSON, an unknown type, a message for a creative that is not on display, a foreign token, a CTA past its TTL, a repeated view, or a sink that threw. rawJson is the message as received (possibly null). Called with no lock held, on the thread that delivered the message, so a subclass may hand the error to the widget synchronously. The default logs a java.util.logging warning; a subclass may route it to the register's own error channel. Must not throw.

    • show

      public final void show(Rendering rendering, ActionSink actions)
      Description copied from interface: Surface
      Draws rendering, replacing anything currently shown, and reports the shopper's interactions with it to actions. The sink is bound to this rendering: a surface hands back the rendering's own Cta instances and never a token it made up.
